title: Baste a roast with a bulb baster held by its bulb: squeeze, dip in the juices, release, carry, squeeze onto the roast
keywords: tool held by its soft end
instruction: Baste the roast with the juices from the pan, then put the baster down on the counter.
context: Basting a roast (pork loin, beef, a chicken or the holiday turkey) with a bulb baster is a common home-kitchen job; the stand-in is pork-loin-sized. The baster is a 12 in tube held only by its soft bulb, and the same squeeze that holds it also works it: squeeze to empty the bulb, put the tip under the shallow juices, ease off so the bulb draws them up, lift out without squeezing, hold the tip over the roast and squeeze. The juices stay in the tube only by the bulb's suction: squeezing on the way drips on the counter, tilting the baster level lets air in and part of the juices run out when it points down again, and letting the bulb open with the tip out of the juices draws air. Squeezed while moving or tilted, the jet carries past the roast, the further the higher the tip.
setup: Positions are in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, with x forward, y to the robot's left and the counter (table) top at z 0. Roasting pan: a Chicago Metallic Professional roast pan, 13 x 9 x 2-1/4 in, its rack left out, long side across the robot, centered at (36.0, 0.0). Roast stand-in: a 9 in length of 4x4 lumber (3.5 x 3.5 in dressed), wrapped in plastic film, lying in the middle of the pan along y. A white wipe-clean vinyl tablecloth covers the counter with the pan standing on it, and tape marks on it show the pan's corners and the baster's outline. Juices: 3 US cups (710 mL) of room-temperature water with a few drops of brown food coloring, standing about 1.3 cm deep around the stand-in. Baster: an OXO Good Grips baster (12 x 2.5 x 2 in, flat silicone bulb, clear Tritan tube, 40 mL), empty and dry, lying flat on the counter to the left of the pan along x, tip toward the robot, its tip at (9.0, 25.0). Both arms start at their ready pose. What is simulated, and how, is in README.md.
scoring: In simulation, juices that land on the roast stand-in's top and on the counter are counted in mL. The trial scores 1.0 when at least 20 mL is on the roast's top, at most 2 mL is on the counter, the pan was never tipped more than 8 degrees, and the baster has been let go resting on the counter outside the pan (lowest point within 5 mm of the counter, moving under 0.3 m/s when let go, not dropped or thrown) with both arms clear of it (in simulation every arm link at least 5 mm from it), all still (under 1 cm/s) for 1 s. It scores 0.75 for the same juices with the baster not yet set down, let go or still; 0.5 for at least 20 mL on the roast with more than 2 and at most 10 mL on the counter; 0.25 for 8 to 20 mL on the roast, or for at least 8 mL on the roast with more than 10 mL on the counter; otherwise 0, including under 8 mL on the roast and the pan tipped past 8 degrees. Doing nothing scores 0. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0. Juices that fall back into the pan count neither way; juices count on the roast only while it is in the pan, top up. Real trial, judged by eye from the overhead and wrist-camera videos and an end photo (an approximation of these rules): 0 if no brown water lands on the stand-in's top, the tube never filled to its first (10 mL) ring, one side of the pan visibly lifts (the pan tips), or nothing is done; 0.25 if water lands on the top but the tube was filled to less than half its 40 mL markings, or a puddle lands on the tablecloth; 0.5 for a baste (tube at least half full, the stream landing on the top) with more than a few drops on the tablecloth; 0.75 with at most a few drops; 1.0 when the baster is then laid on the counter outside the pan, hands off and everything still for 1 s. Nothing is weighed or measured.
reset_notes: About 1 minute: squeeze any water left in the baster back into the pan, wipe its tip and bulb dry and lay it on its tape outline; most of what landed on the stand-in's film-wrapped top has run back into the pan; wipe its top dry so the next trial's landing shows in the video. Wipe the tablecloth dry and top the pan up to its 3-cup fill mark (tape on the pan's outside). Nothing is consumed but a little tap water. A rolled towel in front of the arms' bases dams any spill. The fingers touch only the bulb, above the water; wipe the finger pads if water reached them. In simulation the pan always holds 710 mL and the baster starts empty.
fidelity: Rigid bodies. The flat bulb is a rigid core with four sprung wall panels; a hand squeezes it only by pushing them in. Its suction is a stated law (README): Boyle's law for the air inside, with the wall's spring limiting the vacuum, and the orifice law at the tip, so it draws juices only after a squeeze is released with the tip under the surface. The juices' weight acts on the baster; what leaves the tip falls as a ballistic jet. The bulb's rounded top and corners are drawn only.
